novel_features.name: Unified product card
novel_features.description: See a Q-SYS product's overview, spec-sheet text, configuration pages, and connection guidance in one record.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining the qsys.com product page, its spec-sheet PDF, and the help.qsys.com configuration pages into a single local record - a join that spans two separate websites and a PDF.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this first for any question about a specific model; it answers spec, config, and wiring questions in one call instead of three.

novel_features.name: BOM compatibility check
novel_features.description: Check a whole equipment list against a Q-SYS Designer version and get back what is supported and what is not.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the hardware-compatibility matrix parsed into queryable rows so a list of models can be checked at once; the website presents it as a table you read by eye, one model at a time.
novel_features.example: qsys-pp-cli compat check CX-Q TSC-70-G3 NL-C4 --qds 9.4 --agent
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before quoting or commissioning to catch an unsupported part while it is still cheap to swap.

novel_features.name: Deprecation sweep
novel_features.description: Flag which models in a list are deprecated or discontinued before they reach a quote.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-references deprecation notices against the discontinued-product family list locally; no single page on either site answers this for an arbitrary model list.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to sanity-check a parts list; an end-of-life part caught at design time costs nothing, caught at order time costs a redesign.

novel_features.name: Connection guidance by model
novel_features.description: Get the networking, wiring, and I/O guidance that actually applies to a given model.
novel_features.rationale: Requires resolving a model to its family and then to the relevant subset of networking and wiring pages; the help site presents a flat section the reader filters by hand.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for how-do-I-wire-this-in questions instead of reading the whole networking section.

novel_features.name: BOM sweep — one report per model
novel_features.description: One report per model in an equipment list: version support, EOL status, and spec-sheet availability in a single pass.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining products, the compatibility matrix, and deprecation notices locally; neither QSC site can answer a whole BOM at once.
novel_features.example: qsys-pp-cli bom verify CX-Q TSC-70-G3 NL-C4 --qds 9.4 --agent
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for the complete pre-quote check on a parts list instead of three separate lookups per part.

novel_features.name: Version-aware page reads
novel_features.description: Read a help page as of a specific Q-SYS Designer version from the versioned doc tree.
novel_features.rationale: Requires addressing the versioned doc trees (/q-sys_9.4/, /q-sys_9.6/, /q-sys_10.0/, all verified HTTP 200); the live site shows only the current release, so a 9.4 system is silently documented by 10.x text.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when commissioning a system that runs an older Designer than today's docs describe.

novel_features.name: Extraction coverage report
novel_features.description: Report how many products resolved a spec sheet and how many pages parsed, so extraction gaps are visible.
novel_features.rationale: Only a local index knows what it failed to capture; a website can never tell you what it did not give you.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run this after a harvest; a silent drop in coverage means the vendor changed their HTML and results are now incomplete.

novel_features.name: UC platform integration lookup
novel_features.description: Find which UC platforms (Teams, Zoom, Meet) a device is certified or integrated with.
novel_features.rationale: Requires indexing the 34 Application_Integration pages and matching them to product models locally; no page on either site indexes certifications by device.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when a room design must match the client's chosen UC platform.

narrative.headline: Q-SYS product specs, configuration procedures, and connection guides in one local index - with equipment-list compatibility checks neither QSC website can do.
narrative.value_prop: Q-SYS documentation is split across two sites: qsys.com carries the product spec sheets as PDFs, and help.qsys.com carries the configuration and networking guidance. Neither one can tell you whether a list of equipment runs on a given Designer version. This CLI harvests both into local SQLite, joins them into one record per product, and answers spec, configuration, wiring, and compatibility questions offline - including from a job site with no usable network.

quickstart.comment: confirm the CLI is healthy before syncing anything
build the local corpus from both vendor sites; this is the one slow step
full-text search across every synced page
the unified card: overview, specs, config pages, wiring
check an equipment list against a Designer version
confirm how much of each site actually parsed

troubleshoots.symptom: product get returns no spec text
troubleshoots.fix: Run `qsys-pp-cli coverage` - the product page may not link a spec sheet, and the source PDF URL is still returned.
Run `qsys-pp-cli harvest` first; the corpus is empty until the initial harvest completes.

troubleshoots.symptom: compat check reports a model as unknown
troubleshoots.fix: Model naming varies between the spec sheets and the compatibility matrix; try the series name (CX-Q) rather than a specific SKU (CX-Q 8K8).
Expected - the initial sync walks both sitemaps and fetches spec PDFs. Use `qsys-pp-cli harvest --only products --limit 25` to narrow it.

troubleshoots.symptom: page get --version returns a 404 for a version
troubleshoots.fix: Only released version trees are served (9.4, 9.6, and 10.0 verified); a misspelled or unreleased version 404s from help.qsys.com.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for questions about Q-SYS equipment: what a product's specifications are, how to configure a specific device, how to connect or network it, and whether a set of equipment is supported on a given Q-SYS Designer version. It is built for AV integrators and designers working from an equipment list, and it works offline once harvested, which matters on job sites with locked-down networks.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to control a live Q-SYS Core - it never connects to hardware; use a QRC client library for that
Do not use it to look up control pin names for Lua or QRC scripting - it indexes equipment documentation, not the schematic control surface
Do not treat extracted spec text as authoritative for engineering sign-off - always confirm against the source PDF URL it returns
Do not use it for pricing, availability, or lead times - it indexes documentation only

recipes.title: Check a whole BOM against a Designer version
recipes.explanation: Reads an equipment list from a file on stdin and returns a per-model report: version support, EOL status, and spec-sheet availability.

recipes.title: Narrow a verbose product record for an agent
recipes.explanation: Product records carry full spec-sheet text; --select trims the payload to just the fields needed so an agent does not burn context on prose.

recipes.title: Read docs as an older Designer version saw them
recipes.explanation: A site commissioned on 9.4 reads the 9.4 tree instead of silently getting today's 10.x behavior.

recipes.title: Get wiring guidance for a touchscreen
recipes.explanation: Resolves the model to its family and returns only the networking and wiring pages that apply to it.

recipes.title: Verify the local copy is complete
recipes.explanation: Reports spec-sheet match rate and page parse rate so a silent extraction regression is visible.
